title: Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority (FI) Decides on New Risk Weight Assessment Methodologies for Banking Capital Requirements
originalTitle: Nya metoder för bankernas riskvikter och kapitalkrav beslutade
summary: Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority (FI) (FI) has finalised new supervisory methods for banks' internal models for corporate exposures, requiring PD estimates to assume at least one downturn year in five and introducing a 2.5-year maturity floor for banks using the advanced IRB method; the changes (applied in 2016) will raise risk weights and capital requirements and affect major Swedish banks. title: Fallande dom i mal om grov krigsforbrytelse och terroristbrott
originalTitle: Fällande dom i mål om grov krigsförbrytelse och terroristbrott
summary: Stockholms tingsratt has convicted a 32-year-old Swedish citizen of a gross war crime and terrorist offences for participating in and being filmed at the execution of a Jordanian coalition pilot by IS, and sentenced him to life imprisonment; the judgment references Geneva Conventions, international law, cross‑border prosecution and temporary transfer arrangements with France. The court also awarded damages to the victim's family and discussed complexities relating to prior foreign life sentences and transfer/serving of penalties.

title: Swedish Administrative Court Case No. 2678-22
summary: The Swedish Supreme Administrative Court has referred questions to the EU Court of Justice about whether charging an electric vehicle at a charging station constitutes a supply of goods under the EU VAT Directive (Articles 14.1 & 15.1) and, if so, whether the supply is made by the station operator or by the intermediary company providing the network and billing. The outcome will determine which entity has VAT liability and in which country the supply is taxable.
explanation: Directly relevant (score 5) because the dispute concerns interpretation of the EU VAT Directive which will determine VAT treatment, liability and cross-border taxation for EV charging services — issues that have immediate compliance, registration and financial consequences for the parties involved.

plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Directly relevant (score 5) because the dispute concerns interpretation of the EU VAT Directive which will determine VAT treatment, liability and cross-border taxation for EV charging services — issues that have immediate compliance, registration and financial consequences for the parties involved.
